cause_quote: The new Doctor migration added `if (runtime && runtime !== "openclaw" && runtime !== "auto") { warnings.push(`...runtime ${runtime} inference ownership was left unchanged; no host account was adopted...`); continue; }`, skipping every explicitly selected Codex runtime job.
user_saw: A migrated heartbeat automation on an explicitly set Codex runtime kept failing with 'Automation has no recorded inference account ... or with openclaw doctor --fix', while doctor --fix repeatedly said it left the job unchanged.
summary: Doctor's cron inference-binding migration now passes Codex harness facts to the auth planner and records a stored host-managed account for Codex-runtime jobs, and the refusal text qualifies the Doctor hint.
reasoning: The blanket runtime skip that the fix narrows was written in d277de776 (#172792), the commit that introduced the Doctor migration file; the runner-side refusal for unbound cron runs using a stored profile already applied to every harness since d25a316 (#172590, `runtime: harness.id`), so Codex-runtime jobs that use host OAuth profiles were never recoverable via Doctor. Confidence is medium because I did not separately confirm that the Codex harness resolved a stored profile at d277de776's time, though the fix PR calls the skip a conflation of Codex selection with native ownership.
